founder.name: Helena Gebhart
founder.quote: I spent 8 years searching for my own direction. That's why I know what students really need: not theory tests, but real experience.

items.question: How does the process work?
items.answer: We start with a free initial conversation where Helena gets to know your child. Then we plan trial days at suitable companies together, and after each experience we discuss what fit well and what happens next.

items.question: What does it cost?
items.answer: We're currently in our pilot phase, so guidance is free for families. We want every child to have the chance at real orientation.

items.question: How long does the process take?
items.answer: It varies and depends entirely on your child. Some find clarity after two or three experiences, others need more time. There's no fixed schedule – the process follows your child.

items.question: Does my child already need to know what they want?
items.answer: No, quite the opposite. Most students who come to us don't know yet. That's exactly what we help with: figuring out which tasks truly fit through real experience rather than theory.

items.question: From what age does this make sense?
items.answer: Most of the students we support are between grades 8 and 11. As a rule of thumb: as soon as your child starts thinking about life after school, we can get started together.

founder.name: Helena Gebhart
founder.openingQuote: Work for adults is like play for children - it gives the day meaning

story.heading: Why I do this
story.paragraph1: Sometimes it's the hardest paths that lead us to what we're truly meant to do. My path was shaped by uncertainty. By moments of feeling lost. By the pressure to make the "right" decision – without knowing how. With gaps in my résumé. With a degree I never finished. With the constant question: what actually fits me?
story.paragraph2: It took 8 years to find clarity. 8 years full of internships, job changes, fresh starts, and doubt. Today I know: it didn't have to be that way.
story.paragraph3: That's why I'm building Animo – alongside my full-time job. Because I want to spare others what I went through myself.
